questions.stem: Several clients on a unit develop vomiting and diarrhea, and norovirus is suspected. Which action is most effective?

options.text: Use alcohol-based hand rub only
Use contact precautions, wash hands with soap and water, and clean with a bleach-based disinfectant
Use airborne precautions
Give all clients antibiotics

rationale.correct: Norovirus: contact precautions, soap and water, bleach-based cleaning, exclude ill staff.

perOption.a: Alcohol is less effective against norovirus.
perOption.b: Norovirus is hardy; soap and water and bleach products are recommended.
perOption.c: Norovirus isn't airborne in the usual sense.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance

questions.stem: Place the steps for applying sterile gloves (open method) in order.

items.text: Pull the second glove on and adjust both gloves, touching only sterile surfaces
Pick up the first glove by the folded cuff with the nondominant hand
Slide the dominant hand into the first glove
Perform hand hygiene and open the glove package on a clean, dry surface
Slide the gloved fingers under the cuff of the second glove

perOption.a: Prepares a sterile field.
